messages.body_plain:
On Jun 28, 2008, at 4:55 AM, Agustin Lobo wrote:

> Hi!
>
> Since I upgraded, I get the following message after JGR():
> Creating per-session help links...
> Making links in per-session dir ... done
> Warning message:
> In file.symlink(from, to) :
>   cannot symlink '/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/rJava' to
> '/tmp/RtmpXgqrij/.R/library/rJava.1/rJava', reason 'Permission denied'
>
> is this anything to worry about?
>

It depends. It seems as if you have two rJava packages on your library  
path. Check
.libPaths()
and see whether you have rJava in both. In theory it's harmless, but  
in practice it may be confusing because you don't know which of them  
will have higher priority under different circumstances. You may  
consider removing one of them to avoid confusion. It is usually a good  
idea to install packages either in the system library or in your own  
location, but never in both places. That being said, it is still legal  
to have multiple versions around, but it's confusing and makes  
troubleshooting more difficult.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
On Jul 15, 2008, at 9:01 AM, <c.lieftink at nki.nl> <c.lieftink at nki.nl>  
wrote:

> Hi Simon and others,
>
> Until now I used double[] for transferring data between the Java and  
> the R environment via Rserve. However I have to open up the  
> possibility of Null values in Java which have to be treated as NA in  
> R. what is the most efficient way to deal with this? Do I have to  
> use String[] in stead of the double[] or is there another solution?
>

You can use NaN and convert them to NAs in R if you wish or you can  
use R's NA constant right away (it can be created using  
Double.longBitsToDouble(0x7ff00000000007a2L)). For the latter to work,  
you have to use the most recent Rserve from RForge that assigns NaN is  
raw form.  BTW: for integers you can use the magic NA constant   
-2147483648 (which is in fact INT_MIN).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
I just installed the latest version of JGR on WinXP.
I managed, but there are some problems.
First of all, it tries to install iWidgets from CRAN,
but iWidgets does not seem to be there.

Secondly, I have a setup where all the nonrecommended libraries live in
R_HOME/site-library instead of
R_HOME/library
This makes upgrading to a new version much easier.
R automatically installs new libraries there when this
directory exists. This is documented behavior.
JGR does not find the libraries there and therefore tries to install the 
libraries each time it is started. Then, however, it installs
the packages i site-library and does not find them again.
So I manually had to move
the packages JGR, rJava, JavaGD, and iplots
and i had to install iWidgets from manually after downloadig it from RForge.

Now JGR still hangs at startup. I get the opening screen, but it the 
cursor is the sandclock and the app is nonresponsive.

messages.body_plain:
On Jul 16, 2008, at 10:43 AM, Erich Neuwirth wrote:

> I just installed the latest version of JGR on WinXP.
> I managed, but there are some problems.
> First of all, it tries to install iWidgets from CRAN,
> but iWidgets does not seem to be there.
>

iWidgets were installed in some 1.4 versions I believe, ever since 1.5  
they are optional. In theory they are now superseded by gWidgets, but  
I have hot really tested that setup. Apparently the Windows installer  
was not updated to drop iWidgets on a clean install [unlike OS X and  
Unix]. (However, the failure to install iWidgets is harmless - yet it  
can be installed with "jgr --rforge" which takes all packages from  
RForge instead of CRAN).


> Secondly, I have a setup where all the nonrecommended libraries live  
> in
> R_HOME/site-library instead of
> R_HOME/library
> This makes upgrading to a new version much easier.

[I fail to see how this makes updating easier given how R in installed  
on Windows, but that's another story..]
JGR on Windows doesn't support custom package locations. You have to  
install it in R_HOME/library, there is no choice. If you have a custom  
setup, you have to make sure that all packages are installed in R_HOME/ 
library and you're on your own.

If you still have problems, try removing the JGR preferences file  
(.JGRprefsrc in your HOME).

Cheers,
Simon

You can simply set -Xmx512m or whichever amount you need (see java -X

>> jgr.exe -Xmx512m
>
> Still ends up giving me just 64Mb of RAM.  Is there some explicit  
> way I can call the JVM?
>

Yes, but it's painful (use --debug and have a look at c:/ 
JGRdebug.txt). I'd rather recommend to upgrade to the newest JGR  
launcher (1.61), it supports -Xmx out of the box (and the default is  
512Mb anyway). The binary shoudl be out shortly, otehrwise you can  
build it in launcher/windows of the JGR 1.6-2 package from http://rforge.net/JGR/files/

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Antony,

On Jul 25, 2008, at 6:16 AM, Antony Unwin wrote:

>> package.manager()
> Error in package.manager() :
>   this function is intended to work with the Aqua GUI
>
> This used to happen occasionally.  Currently it seems to happen every
> time, possibly because of this reported masking:
>
> Attaching package: 'utils'
> The following object(s) are masked from package:JGR :
> package.manager
>

Can you, please, share with us the exact version of JGR [see  
sessionInfo()] and the launcher? At any rate you may try to delete  
your preferences (while JGR is not running). Otherwise JGR 1.6-2 (and  
the corresponding new launcher) should (indirectly) address this issue  
as well.


> And while I am at it, can something be done about the following
> warning message:
>
> During startup - Warning messages:
> 1: '.iplots.fw' looks like a pre-2.4.0 S4 object: please recreate it
>

Please remove that object from your workspace rm(.iplots.fw) before  
loading iplots (or remove it, save the workspace and restart). It was  
used by ancient iplots version some years ago, but the current version  
uses different object types.

Best,
Simon
